outcome: respiratory morbidity (respiratory distress syndrome, transient tachypnea of the newborn)
cohort: The study included 12,459 neonates born in KK Women's and Children's Hospital, comprising late preterm infants (34-36 weeks gestation) and term neonates.
finding: Late preterm neonates had significantly higher morbidity and resource utilisation compared to term infants, with 34-week-old infants experiencing greater complications than those born at 35 to 36 weeks.
